name: Aratus of Soli
credit: Portrait: unknown artist — Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Aratus of Soli was a Greek poet of the early third century BC who worked at the court of Antigonus Gonatas of Macedon. He is known above all for the Phaenomena, a didactic hexameter poem on the constellations and on weather signs.

The Phaenomena, based on a prose work by the astronomer Eudoxus, was translated into Latin by Cicero and others and remained a school text for centuries. Mair’s Loeb prose translation (1921) is given in the Works section.

poems.title: Book XI, 437
poems.author: Aratus of Soli
poems.text: I lament for Diotimus, who sits on stones repeating Alpha and Beta to the children of Gargarus.

poems.title: Book XII, 129
poems.author: Aratus of Soli
poems.text: Philoctes of Argos is “fair” at Argos, and the columns of Corinth and tombstones of Megara announce the same. It is written that he is fair as far as Amphiaraus’ Baths. But that is little; they are only letters that beat us. For they are not stones that testify to this Philocles’ beauty, but Rhianus, who saw him with his own eyes, and he is superior to the other one.
